title: [CRY-19] A `RecoveryAssertion` can be replayed; nothing binds it to the identity state it replaces
description: Review finding CRY-19: A `RecoveryAssertion` can be replayed; nothing binds it to the identity state it replaces (lens CRY). Location: spec/02-identity.md:153-163, spec/02-identity.md:243, spec/02-identity.md:467. Fix: Narrow the scope. For self-hosted did:webvh, a replayed assertion changes nothing by itself, because the device key enters the document only through a log entry signed with the update key (02:123). The replay works against the provisioning service, which "accepts a `RecoveryAssertion` as equivalent to an IdP token" (02:467). The assertion is published to discovery (02:163). The recovery key is never rotated after use, and the social-recovery key only "SHOULD" be (02:198), so the old assertion still verifies against the current document. The 24-hour rule at 02:243 bounds the window but does not close it. Fix as proposed: add `prev` (`versionId` or PLC operation CID) and reject an assertion whose `prev` is not the current head. Full text: notes/review/CRY-verified.md and notes/review/CRY.md.
close_reason: FIXED per notes/review/reconciliation.md: spec/02-identity.md §2.4.1 l160/l167 RecoveryAssertion carries `prev` (log versionId); verifiers MUST reject if signature not under recoverableIdentity key at `prev` or `prev` not current log head; §2.5 l484 provisioning service applies same `prev` check
